_comment: FIXED-GEOMETRY CONCEPT ANALYSIS, PRM2 Concept 6, against the RFP THRESHOLD requirements only. Same file format as Turbofan_Sizing (copied from Turbofan_Sizing/prm2_concept6_rfp_requirements.json) plus geometry.S_ref_fixed_ft2. Run with concept_sizing (Concept_Analysis folder): the wing area and every other geometric input are held FIXED and only the takeoff weight is closed by the sizing loop; every requirement is then CHECKED at the resulting design point and the heaviest weight that still meets them is found. Engine F124-GA-100 (fixed), L-39-calibrated weights, training + ferry missions. Keys that start with an underscore are documentation only.
_run_it: From the Concept_Analysis folder: result = concept_sizing('concept6_rfp.json');
_requirements_used: Constraint diagram: RFP-3-P02-R01.1 (+R01.1.1 2 % thrust margin) max speed; RFP-3-P02-R02.1 Ps; RFP-3-P02-R03.1 sustained g; RFP-3-P02-R04.1 takeoff distance; RFP-3-P02-R05.1 critical field length; RFP-3-P02-R06.1 and RFP-1-P02-R01.1 landing / full-stop FCLP. Atmosphere: RFP-3-P01-R01.1 ISA (get_state is the 1976 US Standard Atmosphere below 65,617 ft). Payload: RFP-3-P04-R01, RFP-3-P05-R01. Mission: RFP-3-P09/P10 ferry flight (std_mission) and RFP-3-P07/P08 training flight (documented below, not run). Every other requirement in the set is a deliverable, not a performance constraint.
_team_selected_values: The RFP leaves several conditions to the team (they must be documented in the proposal): reference Mach for Ps and sustained g (M 0.80 used here; 0.70 made the objective design impossible to close), takeoff screen height, landing obstacle height, maximum landing weight, internal fuel fraction (sets the 'MTOW minus 50 % internal fuel' weight), cruise and reserve altitudes. Each is marked TEAM-SELECTED below. This case also fixes: 35,000 ft ferry cruise with 300 ft/min capability, 45,000 ft service ceiling (100 ft/min), and +7 / -3 g instantaneous at 15,000 ft, M 0.70, all TEAM-SELECTED.

geometry._comment_concept: CONCEPT ANALYSIS: S_ref_fixed_ft2 is the concept's reference wing area and is held FIXED (concept_sizing). Span, chords, MAC and the tail areas follow from it and the shape inputs below, so they are fixed too.
geometry._comment: PLACEHOLDER baseline: T-45C-like planform (the RFP's own class), with a supercritical section so the M 0.90 objective is not hopeless. Define your own per RFP-4-P08-R01.1.
geometry._src_planform: PLACEHOLDER: T-45C (P-1231: AR 5.0, taper 0.31, 23.67 deg) rounded to 25 deg for the higher speed target.
geometry._src_thickness_ratio: From the VSP NACA 64A sections: t/c at the side of body (y = 2.25 ft) 0.130, tip 0.050. The code uses their average (0.090) for wetted area and the Korn drag-divergence Mach; the exposed-wing area-weighted mean is 0.084.

horizontal_tail._src: FROM HawkTAconcept6.vsp3: horizontal tail and single vertical tail. Areas (total, both sides): horizontal 74.42 ft^2, vertical 29.50 ft^2. Moment arms = tail chord-weighted quarter-chord x minus the wing's (20.62 ft): L_ht 10.35 ft, L_vt 10.66 ft. Volume coefficients BACKED OUT so TfGeom reproduces the VSP areas exactly at the VSP wing (215.52 ft^2, code MAC 6.371 ft, span 34.94 ft): V_ht = S_ht L_ht / (S MAC) = 0.5609, V_vt = S_vt L_vt / (S b) = 0.04175. In Turbofan_Sizing (wing area varies) the tails then scale with the wing at these coefficients.

vertical_tail._src: FROM HawkTAconcept6.vsp3: horizontal tail and single vertical tail. Areas (total, both sides): horizontal 74.42 ft^2, vertical 29.50 ft^2. Moment arms = tail chord-weighted quarter-chord x minus the wing's (20.62 ft): L_ht 10.35 ft, L_vt 10.66 ft. Volume coefficients BACKED OUT so TfGeom reproduces the VSP areas exactly at the VSP wing (215.52 ft^2, code MAC 6.371 ft, span 34.94 ft): V_ht = S_ht L_ht / (S MAC) = 0.5609, V_vt = S_vt L_vt / (S b) = 0.04175. In Turbofan_Sizing (wing area varies) the tails then scale with the wing at these coefficients.

fuselage._comment: PLACEHOLDER tandem two-seat fuselage with the engine buried (T-45C-like). Two zero-zero seats (RFP-3-P05-R02.1) and the 62-77 in pilot range (RFP-3-P04) set the cockpit; measure your layout.

nacelle._src: Single engine buried in the fuselage (no nacelle wetted area). Change to 'pod' if your concept pods its engine.

geometry._src_taper_ratio: EQUIVALENT straight-tapered wing with the VSP area, span and tip chord: c_root = 2S/b - c_tip = 8.106 ft, c_tip 4.230 ft, taper 0.5218. (The aero report quoted the outboard panel's taper only.)
geometry._src_sweep_quarter_chord_deg: CORRECTED. The VSP sweeps are LEADING-EDGE sweeps (Sweep_Location = 0); the aero report used them as quarter-chord sweeps. Equivalent wing: LE sweep 16.94 deg (tip LE position / semispan), quarter-chord sweep 13.99 deg = atan(tan LE - (c_root - c_tip)/(4 b/2)).
geometry._vsp_source: AVD_CoDR_Aero_data/VSP/HawkTAconcept6.vsp3, 'Wing' component (read by Claude from the XML). Wing sections: y 0.00-1.30 ft: NACA 64A010 (a=0.8) -> NACA 64A010 (a=0.8), chord 7.49->7.29 ft, LE sweep 15.57 deg; y 1.30-1.85 ft: NACA 64A010 (a=0.8) -> NACA 64A213 (a=0.8), chord 7.29->7.21 ft, LE sweep 15.57 deg; y 1.85-4.60 ft: NACA 64A213 (a=0.8) -> NACA 64A213 (a=0.8), chord 7.21->6.79 ft, LE sweep 15.57 deg; y 4.60-10.14 ft: NACA 64A213 (a=0.8) -> NACA 64A206 (a=0.8), chord 6.79->5.95 ft, LE sweep 15.52 deg; y 10.14-10.24 ft: NACA 64A206 (a=0.8) -> NACA 64A206 (a=0.8), chord 5.95->6.56 ft, LE sweep -80.54 deg; y 10.24-17.47 ft: NACA 64A206 (a=0.8) -> NACA 64A205 (a=0.8), chord 6.56->4.23 ft, LE sweep 23.21 deg.

aerodynamics._src_Cfe: Concept 6 report: Cfe = CD0 x Sref / S_wet = 0.015125 x 215.51509 / 1057.33985 = 0.003083 (VSPAERO parasite drag, treated as Mach 0.4).
aerodynamics._src_CD0_reference: Concept 6 report: VSPAERO parasite CD0 0.015125 at Sref 215.51509 ft^2, S_wet 1057.33985 ft^2 (S_wet/Sref 4.906). CHECK VALUE - run_tf_sizing prints the code's own CD0 next to it.
aerodynamics._src_airfoil_type: Conventional confirmed: every wing section in the VSP model is a NACA 64A-series airfoil (a = 0.8 mean line).
aerodynamics._src_CLmax_reference_sweep_deg: CLmax values above are quoted at 25 deg quarter-chord sweep (the baseline). TfAero scales all three by cos(sweep)/cos(25 deg) if the sweep changes (Raymer Sec. 12.4): 35 deg gives about 0.90 x. Remove the key to use CLmax as given at any sweep.
aerodynamics._src_CLmin_clean: PLACEHOLDER most negative clean lift coefficient (at the 25 deg reference sweep; scaled with sweep like CLmax). Sets the -3 g instantaneous wall. A cambered section reaches a smaller |CL| inverted than upright; an aft-loaded SUPERCRITICAL section is typically about -0.6 to -0.8 against +1.3 here, a symmetric section about -CLmax. Get it from your airfoil data (RFP-4-P08-R01.1).
aerodynamics._src_CLmax: The report's own method with the CORRECTED quarter-chord sweep: CLmax_clean = 0.9 x section clmax 1.65 x cos(13.99 deg) = 1.4410; takeoff and landing add the report's increments (+0.3848, +0.5497).
aerodynamics._src_increments: Concept 6 report: flap and gear CD0 increments and Oswald-e flap decrements, as given.
aerodynamics._src_tail_interference_ratio: Scales the tails' share of CD0. Kept at 1.0: Cfe comes from the VSPAERO parasite-drag build-up of this same model (conventional tail, Raymer Q ~ 1.04-1.05 already included).

trim_drag._src: Trim drag, clean configuration only (TfAero.trim_drag): dCD = K[(CL - CL_h)^2 - CL^2] + CL_h^2 S/(pi e_t b_h^2), CL_h = (Cm0_w + CL dh) MAC/L_t, Cm0_w = cm0 A cos^2 L/(A + 2 cos L); b_h = horizontal-tail span from the geometry. cm0_airfoil -0.04: APPROXIMATE value for the NACA 64A213/64A206/64A205 (64A010 inboard, cm0 0) sections - check against section data. cg_minus_wing_ac_over_mac 0.0 and tail_span_efficiency 0.8: PLACEHOLDERS, the same values as concepts 2 and 5 so all four are compared on the same basis. See Turbofan_Sizing/V_TAIL_MODEL.md section 3b.

aerodynamics._comment: Merged from the 'JSON INPUTS ONLY' block of AVD_CoDR_Aero_data/Concept_6_aero.txt (VSPAERO). The code builds its drag as CD0 = Cfe x S_wet/S_ref from its OWN geometry model (so CD0 follows the wing as the loop resizes it) plus K CL^2 with Raymer's Oswald e from AR and leading-edge sweep, plus Korn/Lock wave drag. The VSPAERO polar fits below are kept for reference only - the code does not read them.
aerodynamics._src_oswald: Concept 6 report: clean Oswald e 0.8795, which is Raymer Eq. 12.48/12.49 (the same formula TfAero uses, so the code reproduces it from AR and LE sweep). For comparison the VSPAERO cruise polar's b2 implies e = 1/(pi AR b2) = 0.681.

_vspaero_polars._note: Reference only - not read by the code. CD = b0 + b1 CL + b2 CL^2.

aerodynamics._src_CLmax_report: Report values were 1.3648 / 1.7496 / 1.9146 at a sweep of 23.20815 deg, which was the LE sweep taken as quarter-chord.

propulsion._comment: FIXED, REAL ENGINE: Honeywell/ITEC F124-GA-100, low-bypass, non-afterburning turbofan (Aero L-159). engine_sizing = 'fixed' holds T_SL = n x thrust x (1 - installation loss) every pass and takes the engine weight, length and diameter from fixed_engine instead of Raymer's rubber-engine regression. The lapse and TSFC are still Mattingly's low-bypass correlations (no public F124 deck), with the TSFC scaled to the data-sheet SLS value.

fixed_engine.name: F124-GA-100
fixed_engine._src: ENGINE DATA TABLE supplied by the team (Honeywell section, 'Takeoff Conditions'): F124-GA-100 dry SLS thrust 6,400 lb, SFC 0.810 lb/(lbf hr), FPR not given, OPR 19.4, BPR 0.5, airflow 93.8 lbm/s, weight 1,100 lb, max diameter 36.0 in, fan diameter 23.3 in, length 66.8 in, T/W 5.818, application Aero Vodochody L-159 (dry). CROSS-CHECK, Wikipedia 'Honeywell/ITEC F124' spec block (citing Honeywell and AW&ST Source Book 2009): 6,280 lbf, 1,050 lb dry, BPR 0.49, SFC 0.81, diameter 36 in, but LENGTH 102.1 in - the table's 66.8 in probably excludes the exhaust/nozzle. The length only sizes a nacelle, and the engine here is buried, so it does not affect the result. Thrust is taken as the UNINSTALLED rating.

propulsion._src_n_engines: RFP-3-P02-R05.1 defines the critical field length 'applicable to a single-engine aircraft'. No condition may set oei = true.
propulsion._src_bypass_ratio: Engine table: BPR 0.5 (Wikipedia 0.49). With a fixed engine it only enters through the low-bypass lapse and TSFC choice.
propulsion._src_lapse_model: Mattingly AED 2nd ed. Eq. 2.54b, low-bypass, military (dry) power, normalised to 1 at SLS. No public F124 installed-thrust deck; RFP-4-P06-R02.1 asks for one.
propulsion._src_throttle_ratio: PLACEHOLDER (Mattingly 1.0-1.08 for low bypass). Affects every flight condition; check it against your engine deck.
propulsion._src_tsfc_scale: F124-GA-100 SLS SFC 0.810 (engine table) / Mattingly low-bypass 0.90 at SLS = 0.90. Keeps Mattingly's Mach and altitude trends.
propulsion._src_T_TO_over_T_max_continuous: PLACEHOLDER; not used (every condition and segment uses military power or a drag-matched thrust).
propulsion._src_installation_loss_fraction: PLACEHOLDER 5 % (inlet ducts, bleed, power extraction): installed T_SL = 6,400 x 0.95 = 6,080 lbf. RFP-4-P06-R02.1 requires the losses stated.
propulsion._src_engine_regression: NOT USED with engine_sizing = 'fixed' (kept so the file can be switched back to a rubber engine).

weights._comment: Raymer Table 15.2 fighter-column unit weights for the tails and fuselage, land-based gear 0.033 W0, installed engine 1.3 x bare, WING from Raymer's fighter wing equation anchored at the T-45C (wing_raymer), and the all-else fraction calibrated so the build-up reproduces both the L-39C (exact) and the T-45C (+0.8 %).
weights._src_W_payload: Maximum crew: 2 x (205 lb nude pilot, RFP-3-P04-R01, + 35 lb equipment, RFP-3-P05-R01) = 480 lb. No other payload is defined (RFP-4-P02-R04.1 asks the team to itemize any).
weights._src_landing_gear_fraction: Raymer Table 15.2 land-based fighter 0.033 W0 (no carrier-strength gear, RFP-2-P01-R02.1).
weights._src_unit_weights_and_fractions: Raymer Table 15.2 fighter column for the unit weights and the 1.3 installed-engine factor; 0.033 W0 land-based gear (RFP-2-P01-R02.1 excludes carrier gear). all_else_empty_fraction: see the weights _comment. The WING now uses Raymer's fighter wing equation (wing_weight_method), calibrated at the L-39C; unit_weight_wing_psf is kept for wing_weight_method = 'unit'.
weights._src_statistical_empty: Raymer Table 3.1 jet trainer. Cross-check only.
weights._src_fuel_density: JP-5/JP-8 about 6.8 lb/gal. Wing-volume check only; RFP-3-P06-R01.1 requires ALL mission fuel internal, so the fuselage tanks must hold what the wing cannot.

wing_raymer._src: Raymer Eq. 15.1 (fighter/attack wing): W = 0.0103 K_dw K_vs (W_dg N_z)^0.5 S^0.622 A^0.785 (t/c)_root^-0.4 (1+lambda)^0.05 (cos L_qc)^-1 S_csw^0.04. limit_load_factor 'auto' = the largest positive load factor in THIS file's requirements (RFP-3-P02-R03.1.1 ties the structural limit to the sustained-g requirement): 4.0 g for the RFP thresholds, 6.0 g for the objectives (RFP-3-P02-R03.2), 7.0 g where the team's +7 g instantaneous requirement is present. Ultimate factor 1.5 (RFP-4-P04-R02.1). control_surface_fraction 0.12 PLACEHOLDER (enters to the 0.04 power). calibration_factor 1.1448 = ANCHORED AT THE T-45C: the equation equals the unit method (9 psf x exposed area = 1,265 lb) on the T-45C (13,500 lb, 179.64 ft^2, AR 5.0, taper 0.31, 23.67 deg, t/c 0.102 - CNATRA P-1231) at its limit load factor of +7.33 g (the commonly quoted NATOPS figure - NOT VERIFIED against the NATOPS manual; +8 g would lower every wing by about 4 %). With this wing anchor, all_else_empty_fraction 0.2336 reproduces the L-39C empty weight exactly and the T-45C within +0.8 %.

weights._src_all_else_empty_fraction: CALIBRATED with the T-45C-anchored Raymer wing (wing_raymer): reproducing the L-39C empty weight (7,617 lb at 10,362 lb MTOW, land-based gear 0.033, +8 g) needs 0.2336 -> USED; the T-45C (9,394 lb at 13,500 lb, carrier gear 0.045, +7.33 g) needs 0.2282, so with 0.2336 the T-45C comes out within +0.8 %. One value fits BOTH trainers once the wing weight follows the design - the earlier split (0.1915 land-based vs 0.228 carrier) came from the unit-weight wing under-weighing the L-39's thick, straight, +8 g wing.

sizing._comment: Read by concept_sizing: only W_0 is iterated (S_ref_guess_ft2 is not used - the wing is fixed).
sizing._src_missions: Both RFP design missions are flown every pass; the fuel of the one that needs more is carried (RFP-3-P06-R01.1).
sizing._src_guesses: Start ABOVE about 12,600 lb: below that the closure has no solution (the training mission's fuel plus the empty weight exceed W_TO), and a first pass there stops the loop. 15,000 lb / 240 ft^2 converges. S_ref guess = the Concept 6 VSPAERO reference area (215.51509 ft^2); the loop still picks its own wing.

constraints._comment: RFP-3-P02 THRESHOLD requirements only (the minimum the RFP requires). Reference Mach for Ps and sustained g: 0.80 (TEAM-SELECTED; the RFP leaves it to the team). Weight basis MTOW minus 50 % internal fuel = beta 0.89 (PLACEHOLDER fuel fraction).
constraints._condition_keys: type: takeoff | landing | approach_speed | instantaneous_turn | climb_gradient | flight. See get_con.
constraints._src_W_TO_estimate_lbf: PLACEHOLDER first estimate: T-45C MTOW (13,500 lb) less carrier gear, hook and strengthening. Turns T/W into a thrust in run_tf_constraints; the full sizing loop computes its own.

design_point._src: W/S = W_TO_estimate / Concept 6 Sref (215.51509 ft^2). T/W is replaced by the F124's at that weight. The sizing loop picks the smallest wing the engine allows, which can differ from the concept's.

conditions.name: Takeoff 5,000 ft (R04.1)
conditions._src: RFP-3-P02-R04.1: total distance to the screen height <= 5,000 ft at MTOW, 5,000 ft density altitude (= 5,000 ft ISA altitude), zero wind, dry runway, takeoff thrust (R04.1.1). Modelled with Roskam's FAR 25 correlation s = 37.5 TOP25 with sigma at 5,000 ft and the static thrust lapse there. That correlation is a BALANCED field length (it includes an engine failure), so for this all-engines distance it is CONSERVATIVE; replace with a ground-roll + air-distance calculation (Raymer Sec. 17.8) for the proposal.

conditions.name: Critical field 6,000 ft (R05.1)
conditions._src: RFP-3-P02-R05.1: critical field length <= 6,000 ft at MTOW, 5,000 ft density altitude, MIL-STD-3013B single-engine definition (accelerate to the decision speed, then either take off or stop). Approximated with the same balanced-field correlation. With this correlation it is always weaker than the 5,000 ft takeoff line (same slope, longer distance); a proper accelerate-stop calculation with your brake coefficient (R06.1.1) could make it the stronger one.

conditions.name: Landing 5,000 ft (R06.1)
conditions._src: RFP-3-P02-R06.1 (and the full-stop FCLP capability, RFP-1-P02-R01.1): land from the obstacle to a full stop in <= 5,000 ft at MLW, 5,000 ft density altitude, wheel brakes, no arresting gear. distance_is_actual = true converts this ACTUAL distance to the equivalent FAR 25 field length (/0.6) before Roskam's s_FL = 0.3 V_A^2, V_A = 1.3 Vs. beta = MLW/MTOW = 0.88 is TEAM-SELECTED (PLACEHOLDER).

conditions.name: Max speed M0.78 25k ft (R01.1)
conditions._src: RFP-3-P02-R01.1: level flight at M 0.78, 25,000 ft, ISA, military power, clean, MTOW minus 50 % internal fuel. RFP-3-P02-R01.1.1 adds a 2 % thrust margin (T >= 1.02 D): modelled as throttle = 1/1.02 = 0.9804, i.e. the drag must be met with 98 % of the available thrust.

conditions.name: Ps 90 ft/s 15k ft (R02.1)
conditions._src: RFP-3-P02-R02.1: Ps >= 90 ft/s at 15,000 ft, 1 g, military power, MTOW minus 50 % internal fuel. Reference Mach 0.80 is TEAM-SELECTED (the RFP leaves it to the team). Raised from 0.70: at 0.70 the objective 6 g turn pulled the wing loading down to about 36 psf and the objective design could not close; at 0.80 the turn bucket moves to higher W/S and the low-bypass engine has more thrust. Document this choice in the proposal.

conditions.name: Sustained 4.0 g 15k ft (R03.1)
conditions._src: RFP-3-P02-R03.1: level constant-Mach turn at +4.0 g without losing speed (Ps = 0), 15,000 ft, military power, MTOW minus 50 % internal fuel. Same TEAM-SELECTED reference Mach 0.80 as the Ps condition. Where 4 g needs more than the clean CLmax the curve goes off the top of the diagram.

std_mission._description: FERRY FLIGHT, RFP-3-P09 / P10, at 35,000 ft. Segments 1, 2 and 6 use fixed_thrust because the RFP gives them as time at a thrust setting. Reserve: 45 min at maximum-endurance speed (loiter with no speed given).
std_mission._src_reserve: 1 % unusable/trapped fuel (RFP-3-P06-R01.1.1), PLACEHOLDER. The 45-minute reserve is the last segment.
std_mission._src_segments: 1: RFP-3-P09-R01, 15 min idle. PLACEHOLDER idle fuel flow 400 lb/hr: no F124 idle data available; about 8 % of the military fuel flow (6,400 lbf x 0.81 = 5,180 lb/hr), typical of a small turbofan at ground idle. Replace with engine data (RFP-3-P07-R01.1 asks for the team-defined idle fuel flow). 2: RFP-3-P09-R02, 1 min at takeoff (military) thrust at an average M 0.2. 3-4: RFP-3-P09-R03/R04, 35,000 ft and M 0.72 TEAM-SELECTED; RFP-3-P09-R06.1 counts climb and descent distance in the 600 nm, the code counts only the cruise, so 540 nm is used - set it to 600 minus the printed climb distance and about 30 nm of descent. 5: RFP-3-P09-R05, fixed fraction 0.990 (Roskam). 6: RFP-3-P09-R07, 10 min of approach and landing, landing configuration, thrust = level drag at 1.3 V_s (no go-around, per R07.1). 7: RFP-3-P10-R01, 45 min at maximum-endurance speed (L/D max) in cruise configuration; 10,000 ft TEAM-SELECTED.
std_mission._note_rfp_case: The ferry cruise altitude (35,000 ft) is a team choice the RFP allows (RFP-3-P09-R03.1). Without the cruise-capability constraint nothing guarantees the engine can climb there, but the fixed F124 has ample thrust for it.

training_mission._description: TRAINING FLIGHT, RFP-3-P07 / P08: idle taxi, takeoff, climb to 20,000 ft, 50 nm out, idle descent to 10,000 ft, 30 min of military-thrust maneuvering at M 0.60, climb back to 20,000 ft, 50 nm back, idle descent, 30 min of FCLP touch-and-goes, 30 min reserve.
training_mission._src_reserve: 1 % unusable/trapped fuel, PLACEHOLDER. The 30-minute reserve is the last segment.
training_mission._src_segments: 1: RFP-3-P07-R01, 15 min idle. PLACEHOLDER idle fuel flow 400 lb/hr: no F124 idle data available; about 8 % of the military fuel flow (6,400 lbf x 0.81 = 5,180 lb/hr), typical of a small turbofan at ground idle. Replace with engine data (RFP-3-P07-R01.1 asks for the team-defined idle fuel flow). 2: RFP-3-P07-R02, 1 min takeoff thrust, average M 0.2. 3: RFP-3-P07-R03, climb to 20,000 ft at 250 KCAS (taken as KEAS - they differ by under 2 % here); 'mach' 0.85 is only a cap, never reached. 4: RFP-3-P07-R04, 50 nm out at 20,000 ft and M 0.65 (TEAM-SELECTED speed); the climb distance is not subtracted (conservative). 5: RFP-3-P07-R05, idle descent 20,000 -> 10,000 ft, about 4 min at roughly 2,500 ft/min. 6: RFP-3-P07-R06, 30 min at 10,000 ft, M 0.60, MILITARY thrust - flown as one steady condition (the maneuver mix is not modelled; at constant military thrust the fuel does not depend on it). 7-8: RFP-3-P07-R07/R08, climb back to 20,000 ft at 250 KCAS and cruise the same 50 nm back. 9: RFP-3-P07-R09, idle descent to sea level, about 7 min. 10: RFP-3-P07-R10, 30 min of FCLP touch-and-goes, gear down and landing flaps, at 1.3 V_s (TEAM-SELECTED approach speed); thrust = 1.3 x level drag to cover the climbs and accelerations of the circuit (PLACEHOLDER drag_factor - a power-setting time history of a real pattern would replace it). 11: RFP-3-P08-R01, 30 min at maximum-endurance speed in cruise configuration; 10,000 ft TEAM-SELECTED.

_vsp_note: Geometry updated from the OpenVSP model: corrected quarter-chord sweep, VSP thickness ratios, equivalent taper, wing area and AR.
